paper.title_en: Universal relations in Bose gases with power-law interactions in two and three dimensions
paper.abstract_en: We derive universal relations between thermodynamic quantities and the pair distribution function for bosons interacting via repulsive power-law potentials in the dilute regime in three and two dimensions. In particular, we obtain an explicit relation between the potential energy and Tan's contact, for which we also find beyond-mean-field expressions, and establish new connections between the chemical potential and the potential energy per particle, characteristic of systems with finite-range interactions. We perform quantum Monte Carlo simulations in order to verify up to what extent the relation between Tan's contact and the chemical potential holds in three- and two-dimensional systems. The obtained results are relevant for dipoles, quadrupoles, Rydberg atoms, excitons, and other systems in the dilute limit.
